claims.text: `pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
The `pulumi import` CLI command accepts a syntax of the form `pulumi import <type>:<module>/<resource>:<Resource> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
The `@pulumi/policy` package exports a `PolicyPack` construct and a `validateResourceOfType` function.
A Pulumi `PolicyPack` can define a `require-tags` policy with `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` that validates `aws.ec2.Instance` resources for required tags.
`aws.ec2.Instance` resources expose a `tags` property that can be inspected via `validateResourceOfType`.
`aws.s3.Bucket` resources expose an `acl` property that can take values such as `"public-read"` or `"public-read-write"`.
The `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` module exports a `LocalWorkspace` class with a `createOrSelectStack` method.
`LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` accepts a configuration object with `stackName`, `projectName`, and a `program` function.
A Pulumi Automation API stack object has a `setConfig` method that can set configuration values such as `aws:region`.
A Pulumi Automation API stack object has an `up` method that accepts an `onOutput` callback and returns a result containing `outputs`.
Pulumi's `ComponentResource` class can be extended to create custom reusable components.
A `ComponentResource` subclass constructor calls `super()` with a type token, name, empty args object, and options.
`aws.lb.LoadBalancer` accepts arguments including `name`, `loadBalancerType`, `subnets`, and `internal`.
`aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` accepts arguments including `family`, `networkMode`, `requiresCompatibilities`, `cpu`, `memory`, and `containerDefinitions`.
`aws.ecs.Service` accepts arguments including `cluster`, `taskDefinition`, `desiredCount`, `launchType`, and `networkConfiguration`.
A `ComponentResource` subclass should call `this.registerOutputs()` with an object of output properties.

The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches readers to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi when beneficial, and orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Pulumi's `pulumi.StackReference` class has a `getOutput` method that can retrieve outputs such as a VPC ID from another stack.

There exists a `terraform.state.S3Reference` construct (in a `@pulumi/terraform`-like package) that can reference Terraform state stored in an S3 bucket by bucket and key, and expose a `getOutput` method to retrieve individual state outputs.
